cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Reconciliation ≠ Estrangement – the restoration of friendly relations.

p.em: Example: Reconciliation requires willingness from both sides.

cosy-blockquote.p: Forgiveness ≠ Resentment – the action or process of forgiving or being forgiven.

p.em: Example: Forgiveness brings emotional relief and peace of mind.

cosy-blockquote.p: Grudge ≠ Goodwill – a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment.

p.em: Example: Holding a grudge only hurts the person carrying it.

cosy-blockquote.p: Apology ≠ Defiance – a regretful acknowledgment of an offense or failure.

p.em: Example: A sincere apology can heal years of misunderstanding.

cosy-blockquote.p: Empathy ≠ Apathy – the ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

p.em: Example: Empathy helps us see conflict from the other person's point of view.

cosy-blockquote.p: Compromise ≠ Intransigence – an agreement reached by mutual concession.

p.em: Example: Healthy relationships rely on honest compromise.

cosy-blockquote.p: Rapport ≠ Discord – a close and harmonious relationship.

p.em: Example: Building rapport takes time and open communication.

cosy-blockquote.p: Mediator ≠ Instigator – a person who attempts to make people involved in a conflict come to an agreement.

p.em: Example: A neutral mediator can help resolve family disputes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vulnerability ≠ Defensiveness – the quality of being open to emotional exposure.

p.em: Example: Showing vulnerability is a sign of courage, not weakness.
Example: Restoring harmony in a team improves everyone's wellbeing.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why is reconciliation often difficult after a long period of holding a grudge?
★ Looking back at a past argument, what should you have done differently to resolve it sooner?

How does offering a sincere apology help restore emotional harmony?
★ What makes an apology feel genuine to you?

What role does empathy play in reaching a fair compromise during an argument?
★ How do you calm down when an argument gets heated?

Why does showing emotional vulnerability build stronger rapport between people?
★ Who in your life do you feel most comfortable being open with?

When can a neutral mediator help resolve persistent disagreements?
★ Have you ever helped two friends make peace with each other?

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:

★ Do you think holding a grudge could have been avoided if both parties spoke openly earlier?

How can workplace culture encourage healthier conflict resolution and reconciliation?
★ How are disagreements handled in your workplace or university?

Can true forgiveness exist without a full verbal apology?
★ Have you ever forgiven someone who never apologized?

★ What activity helps you let go of stress and anger?

What is the most effective way to rebuild trust and long-term harmony after a betrayal?
★ What advice would you give to a friend trying to repair a relationship?
